audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for wilderness grumbling, manna/quail, daily portion, Sabbath rhythm, omer memorial.

verses.restored: They journeyed from Elim, and all congregation of children of Israel came to wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai, on fifteenth day of second month after their going out from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.

modern.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

original.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵילִ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ כָּל עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל מִדְבַּר סִ֔ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּין אֵילִ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין סִינָ֑י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לְצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: All congregation of children of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

familiar.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness:

modern.text: And there in the desert they all grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

original.text: וילינו כָּל עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַל מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְעַֽל אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: Children of Israel said to them, If only we had died by hand of YHWH in land of Egypt, when we sat by pots of flesh and ate bread to fullness; for you brought us out to this wilderness to kill all this assembly with hunger.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.

modern.text: “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִֽי יִתֵּ֨ן מוּתֵ֤נוּ בְיַד יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּ֨נוּ֙ עַל סִ֣יר הַבָּשָׂ֔ר בְּאָכְלֵ֥נוּ לֶ֖חֶם לָשֹׂ֑בַע כִּֽי הוֹצֵאתֶ֤ם אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְהָמִ֛ית אֶת כָּל הַקָּהָ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בָּרָעָֽב

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Look, I am raining bread for you from heavens; the people shall go out and gather a day's matter in its day, so I may test them whether they walk in my Torah/instruction or not.

familiar.text: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מַמְטִ֥יר לָכֶ֛ם לֶ֖חֶם מִן הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְיָצָ֨א הָעָ֤ם וְלָֽקְטוּ֙ דְּבַר י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ לְמַ֧עַן אֲנַסֶּ֛נּוּ הֲיֵלֵ֥ךְ בְּתוֹרָתִ֖י אִם לֹֽא

verses.restored: On sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it shall be double what they gather day by day.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, that on the sixth day they shall prepare that which they bring in; and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.

modern.text: Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”

original.text: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י וְהֵכִ֖ינוּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר יָבִ֑יאוּ וְהָיָ֣ה מִשְׁנֶ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר יִלְקְט֖וּ י֥וֹם יֽוֹם

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron said to all children of Israel, Evening, then you shall know that YHWH brought you out from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And Moses and Aaron said unto all the children of Israel, At even, then ye shall know that the LORD hath brought you out from the land of Egypt:

modern.text: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן אֶֽל כָּל בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֶ֕רֶב וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י יְהוָ֛ה הוֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: And morning, then you shall see glory of YHWH, because he hears your grumblings against YHWH. And what are we, that you grumble against us?

familiar.text: And in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of the LORD; for that he heareth your murmurings against the LORD: and what are we, that ye murmur against us?

modern.text: and in the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we that you should grumble against us?”

original.text: וּבֹ֗קֶר וּרְאִיתֶם֙ אֶת כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה בְּשָׁמְע֥וֹ אֶת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם עַל יְהוָ֑ה וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה כִּ֥י תלונו עָלֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Moses said, When YHWH gives you flesh in evening to eat and bread in morning to fullness, because YHWH hears your grumblings that you grumble against him; what are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against YHWH.

familiar.text: And Moses said, This shall be, when the LORD shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that the LORD heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the LORD.

modern.text: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּתֵ֣ת יְהוָה֩ לָכֶ֨ם בָּעֶ֜רֶב בָּשָׂ֣ר לֶאֱכֹ֗ל וְלֶ֤חֶם בַּבֹּ֨קֶר֙ לִשְׂבֹּ֔עַ בִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ יְהוָה֙ אֶת תְּלֻנֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עָלָ֑יו וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה לֹא עָלֵ֥ינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם כִּ֥י עַל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Moses said to Aaron, Say to all congregation of children of Israel, Draw near before YHWH, for he has heard your grumblings.

familiar.text: And Moses spake unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before the LORD: for he hath heard your murmurings.

modern.text: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֱמֹ֗ר אֶֽל כָּל עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קִרְב֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע אֵ֖ת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: As Aaron spoke to all congregation of children of Israel, they turned toward wilderness, and look, glory of YHWH appeared in cloud.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as Aaron spake unto the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they looked toward the wilderness, and, behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.

modern.text: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל כָּל עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּפְנ֖וּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה נִרְאָ֖ה בֶּעָנָֽן

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר

verses.restored: I have heard grumblings of children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, Between the evenings you shall eat flesh, and in morning you shall be satisfied with bread; and you shall know that I am YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak unto them, saying, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I am the LORD your God.

modern.text: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”

original.text: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בֵּ֤ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֨יִם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ בָשָׂ֔ר וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ לָ֑חֶם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: It happened in evening that quail came up and covered the camp, and in morning there was layer of dew around the camp.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.

modern.text: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַתַּ֣עַל הַשְּׂלָ֔ו וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּבַבֹּ֗קֶר הָֽיְתָה֙ שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטַּ֔ל סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה

verses.restored: The layer of dew went up, and look, upon face of wilderness, a fine flaky thing, fine like frost on earth.

familiar.text: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground.

modern.text: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.

original.text: וַתַּ֖עַל שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטָּ֑ל וְהִנֵּ֞ה עַל פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּדְבָּר֙ דַּ֣ק מְחֻסְפָּ֔ס דַּ֥ק כַּכְּפֹ֖ר עַל הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Children of Israel saw and said each to one's brother, What is it? For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, It is bread that YHWH has given you to eat.

familiar.text: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.

modern.text: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.

original.text: וַיִּרְא֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל אָחִיו֙ מָ֣ן ה֔וּא כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ מַה ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם ה֣וּא הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה

verses.restored: This is the word that YHWH commanded: Gather from it, each according to one's eating, an omer per head, according to number of your souls/lives; each shall take for those in one's tent.

familiar.text: This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons; take ye every man for them which are in his tents.

modern.text: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’”

original.text: זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לִקְט֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ עֹ֣מֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּ֗לֶת מִסְפַּר֙ נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאָהֳל֖וֹ תִּקָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: Children of Israel did so, and they gathered, some more and some less.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.

modern.text: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵ֖ן בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּלְקְט֔וּ הַמַּרְבֶּ֖ה וְהַמַּמְעִֽיט

verses.restored: They measured by omer; the one gathering much had no excess, and the one gathering little had no lack. Each gathered according to one's eating.

familiar.text: And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.

modern.text: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.

original.text: וַיָּמֹ֣דּוּ בָעֹ֔מֶר וְלֹ֤א הֶעְדִּיף֙ הַמַּרְבֶּ֔ה וְהַמַּמְעִ֖יט לֹ֣א הֶחְסִ֑יר אִ֥ישׁ לְפִֽי אָכְל֖וֹ לָקָֽטוּ

verses.restored: Moses said to them, Let no one leave any of it until morning.

familiar.text: And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.

modern.text: Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֕ישׁ אַל יוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד בֹּֽקֶר

verses.restored: But they did not listen to Moses; some left from it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. Moses was angry with them.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.

modern.text: But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.

original.text: וְלֹא שָׁמְע֣וּ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיּוֹתִ֨רוּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עַד בֹּ֔קֶר וַיָּ֥רֻם תּוֹלָעִ֖ים וַיִּבְאַ֑שׁ וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף עֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: They gathered it morning by morning, each according to one's eating; when sun grew hot, it melted.

familiar.text: And they gathered it every morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted.

modern.text: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away. The Sabbath Observed (Genesis 2:1–3; Hebrews 4:1–11)

original.text: וַיִּלְקְט֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ וְחַ֥ם הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְנָמָֽס

verses.restored: On sixth day they gathered double bread, two omers for one; all leaders of congregation came and told Moses.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

modern.text: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person —and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗י לָֽקְט֥וּ לֶ֨חֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥י הָעֹ֖מֶר לָאֶחָ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ כָּל נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיַּגִּ֖ידוּ לְמֹשֶֽׁה

verses.restored: He said to them, This is what YHWH spoke: Tomorrow is Sabbath-rest, holy Sabbath to YHWH. Bake what you bake and boil what you boil, and all surplus set aside for yourselves to keep until morning.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, This is that which the LORD hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.

modern.text: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁבָּת֧וֹן שַׁבַּת קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה מָחָ֑ר אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד הַבֹּֽקֶר

verses.restored: They set it aside until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink, and worm was not in it.

familiar.text: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.

modern.text: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.

original.text: וַיַּנִּ֤יחוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד הַבֹּ֔קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְלֹ֣א הִבְאִ֔ישׁ וְרִמָּ֖ה לֹא הָ֥יְתָה בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Moses said, Eat it today, for today is Sabbath to YHWH; today you will not find it in field.

familiar.text: And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the LORD: to day ye shall not find it in the field.

modern.text: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אִכְלֻ֣הוּ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּֽי שַׁבָּ֥ת הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָ֑ה הַיּ֕וֹם לֹ֥א תִמְצָאֻ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: Six days you shall gather it, but on seventh day, Sabbath, there will be none in it.

familiar.text: Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

modern.text: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”

original.text: שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים תִּלְקְטֻ֑הוּ וּבַיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֛י שַׁבָּ֖ת לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: It happened on seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.

modern.text: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י יָצְא֥וּ מִן הָעָ֖ם לִלְקֹ֑ט וְלֹ֖א מָצָֽאוּ

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, How long do you refuse to keep my commands and my Torah/instructions?

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה עַד אָ֨נָה֙ מֵֽאַנְתֶּ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתַ֖י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי

verses.restored: See, because YHWH has given you Sabbath, therefore on sixth day he gives you bread of two days; sit each under oneself; let no one go out from one's place on seventh day.

familiar.text: See, for that the LORD hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

modern.text: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”

original.text: רְא֗וּ כִּֽי יְהוָה֮ נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֣ם הַשַּׁבָּת֒ עַל כֵּ֠ן ה֣וּא נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י לֶ֣חֶם יוֹמָ֑יִם שְׁב֣וּ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֗יו אַל יֵ֥צֵא אִ֛ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי

verses.restored: So the people rested on seventh day.

modern.text: So the people rested on the seventh day. The Jar of Manna

original.text: וַיִּשְׁבְּת֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי

verses.restored: House of Israel called its name manna; it was like coriander seed, white, and its taste like wafers with honey.

familiar.text: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.

modern.text: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

original.text: וַיִּקְרְא֧וּ בֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ מָ֑ן וְה֗וּא כְּזֶ֤רַע גַּד֙ לָבָ֔ן וְטַעְמ֖וֹ כְּצַפִּיחִ֥ת בִּדְבָֽשׁ

verses.restored: Moses said, This is the word YHWH commanded: Fill an omer from it to keep throughout your generations, so they may see the bread with which I fed you in wilderness when I brought you out from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.

modern.text: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה מְלֹ֤א הָעֹ֨מֶר֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן יִרְא֣וּ אֶת הַלֶּ֗חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶאֱכַ֤לְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּהוֹצִיאִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Moses said to Aaron, Take one jar and put there a full omer of manna, and place it before YHWH to keep throughout your generations.

familiar.text: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept for your generations.

modern.text: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֚ח צִנְצֶ֣נֶת אַחַ֔ת וְתֶן שָׁ֥מָּה מְלֹֽא הָעֹ֖מֶר מָ֑ן וְהַנַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: As YHWH commanded Moses, Aaron placed it before the testimony to keep.

familiar.text: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.

modern.text: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

original.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיַּנִּיחֵ֧הוּ אַהֲרֹ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדֻ֖ת לְמִשְׁמָֽרֶת

verses.restored: Children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to border of land of Canaan.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.

modern.text: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת הַמָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד בֹּאָ֖ם אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת אֶת הַמָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד בֹּאָ֕ם אֶל קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.

familiar.text: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.

modern.text: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)

original.text: וְהָעֹ֕מֶר עֲשִׂרִ֥ית הָאֵיפָ֖ה הֽוּא

translation_notes: Manna asks 'what is it?' and trains daily dependence rather than hoarding.
The omer equality line is central: much had no excess, little had no lack.
Sabbath appears as gift before Sinai law code: rest is liberation practice.
safety_note: Do not frame grumbling as simple moral failure; hunger and wilderness insecurity are real. The chapter forms trust through provision, equality, and Sabbath rest.
